title: Two-dimensional arrays
learningGoals: make a table with rows and columns
read an item with two indexes

youtube.title: C++ 2D Arrays: Rows and Columns | C++ Programming EP 33
youtube.description: In this episode you will make a table with rows and columns, read an item with two indexes and loop over a grid, with Xecxec the crab. 0:00 Intro · 0:15 Two-dimensional arrays · 0:49 A small grid · 1:29 Rows in memory · 1:59 Second program · 2:59 Recap · 3:29 Bug of the Day · 4:17 Challenge · 4:38 Next episode

thumbnail.visual: big text "2D ARRAYS" in tomato on butter; Xecxec next to a cinema seat plan with rows and columns; thin black border and drop shadow.
thumbnail.pose: Xecxec next to a cinema seat plan with rows and columns

scenes.animation: Tomato title card: EP sticker thuds in, title stamps with a whoosh, Xecxec scuttles in and waves; thud, whoosh, claw-click, sting
scenes.narration: Today we make a table. A two-dimensional array has rows and columns, like a cinema seat plan.

scenes.onScreen: "Two-dimensional arrays": numbered lines (1. A 2D array is an array of rows; 2. Two indexes: row first, then column; 3. Use nested loops to visit every cell) and an analogy card: a cinema seat plan: you need a row and a seat number
scenes.animation: Lines spring in one by one with a pop; the analogy card slides in from the right
scenes.narration: A two-dimensional array is an array of rows. Each row is an array of columns. You need two indexes. The first is the row, and the second is the column. In memory, the rows sit one after another. Think of a cinema seat plan. To find your seat, you need a row and a seat number.
points: A 2D array is an array of rows
Two indexes: row first, then column
Use nested loops to visit every cell

analogy.title: Two-dimensional arrays
analogy.body: A cinema seat plan: you need a row and a seat number

scenes.onScreen: seats.cpp: a grid with two rows and three columns
scenes.animation: Code types in with key-tick; butter [HL n] highlight sweeps line by line with marker-swipe; explanation card on the right
scenes.narration: [HL 5] Two rows and three columns. Each inner pair of braces is one row. [HL 6] Row zero, column two is the number three. [HL 7] Row one, column zero is the number four.

scenes.onScreen: six int boxes in a row: row zero first, then row one
scenes.animation: Boxes pop in one by one with size and address tags; arrows draw on as the narrator mentions them; regions are labelled; pop per box
scenes.narration: In memory, the grid is one long row of six boxes. Row zero is the first three. Row one is the next three. The computer finds a cell with the sum row times three plus column.

scenes.onScreen: rowsum.cpp: nested loops add each row
scenes.animation: Second program or a twist on the first; [HL n] and [TRACK name=value] cues drive the variable tracker; output panel fills line by line with a ding per line
scenes.narration: [HL 6] The outer loop picks the row. [HL 7] Each row starts with a new sum of zero. [HL 8] The inner loop visits the three columns. [HL 9] Each cell is added to the sum. [HL 11] Row zero sums to six. Row one sums to fifteen.

scenes.animation: Dark-blue terminal: the compile command types with key-tick, the run command types, output prints in mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Save the file as rowsum dot cpp. Compile it with g plus plus. Then run the program. The program prints Row zero colon six, and Row one colon fifteen.

scenes.animation: Recap lines tick in one by one with a pop; Xecxec nods after each tick
scenes.narration: Let us recap. One. A two-dimensional array has rows and columns. Two. Use the row index first, then the column index. Three. Nested loops visit every cell. Four. Only the first size may be left out. Pause the video. Say these ideas out loud, one time, slowly.
points: A two-dimensional array has rows and columns.
Use the row index first, then the column index.
Only the first size may be left out.

scenes.onScreen: BUG OF THE DAY: A missing column size
scenes.animation: Butter banner drops in with a buzzer; wrong code shakes; the g++ error lines appear in tomato; the fix slides in and the terminal turns mint with a ding
scenes.narration: Bug of the Day. Both sizes are empty. The compiler says multidimensional array must have bounds for all dimensions except the first. It can count the rows from your list. But it needs the column size. Write the number two in the second brackets.

scenes.onScreen: I made a grid of jokes. Every row had a punchline, and every column had a groan.
scenes.animation: Full tomato screen, card flips in with a rimshot, Xecxec snaps his claw
scenes.narration: I made a grid of jokes. Every row had a punchline, and every column had a groan.

scenes.onScreen: Task card: print a multiplication grid
scenes.animation: Task card pops in; checklist ticks with a pop; Xecxec holds a tiny pen
scenes.narration: Your challenge: Make a two by two grid with the numbers one, two, three and four. Print the diagonal: row zero column zero, and row one column one. Write your answer in the comments.

scenes.animation: Next-episode card slides up with a whoosh; right side stays empty for end-screen elements; sign-off text types in
scenes.narration: Next time: std array. Keep coding, says Xecxec!

bug.error:
Compiler output (exactly as g++ prints it):

seats.cpp: In function 'int main()':
seats.cpp:5:9: error: declaration of 'grid' as multidimensional array must have bounds for all dimensions except the first
    5 |     int grid[][] = {{1, 2}, {3, 4}};
      |         ^~~~
bug.why: The compiler can count the rows from your list. It needs the column size to find the start of each row.

pun: "I made a grid of jokes. Every row had a punchline, and every column had a groan."
challenge: Make a two by two grid with the numbers one, two, three and four. Print the diagonal: row zero column zero, and row one column one.
challengeAnswer: Use int grid with two by two braces. Print grid at zero zero, which is one, and grid at one one, which is four.
